trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Consultant: Occupational Health & Safety (Contractor OHS)
Company: Absa Group
About the company: With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Purpose of the role: Implementation, monitoring and auditing of Environment, Health and Safety policy, standards and controls within the Absa Group (specifically focused on Absa Building Contractors)
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Ensure compliance with OHS standards and legislation.
  - Monitor the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) standards and management information system (MIS) by obtaining quarterly reports from all Absa workplaces.
  - Assist regions to become and remain compliant by sending reminders of information that is still outstanding and escalate non-compliance to relevant management structures.
  - Liaise with Business Units by providing expert opinions, advice and recommendations pertaining to the OHS Act and COID (Compensation of Injuries and Diseases on duty).
  - Engage with various internal Business Units as CRES, Regional Operations, Group Wellness, Human Capital and Group Learning to ensure participation and elimination of risks e.g. noise levels, facility related hazards etc.
  - Provide input for training material and present training courses if necessary. Provide facilitators with information when facilitators are not able to respond to a learner’s question. Assist in-country consultants to engage training vendors for courses required for upskilling purposes.
  - Conduct site inspections and investigations (e.g. injury on duty investigations) to identify OHS risk related shortcomings and to ensure procedural compliance by staff and contractors. Submit a report on findings. Analyse investigation reports issued by in-country consultants and/or authorities.
  - Conduct OHS audits and proactive inspections and report on findings with appropriate recommendations to enhance OHS compliance, which could include, technology, procedural, training or even disciplinary action. Submit a report to the workplace and other affected parties.
  - Attend to business unit or region specific meetings and ensure OHS requirements are highlighted and addressed. Attend country legislated OHS Committee Meetings and provide feedback on OHS Compliance from a Centre perspective.
  - Assist with development and revision of policies, procedures and standards.
  - Assist in-country OHS consultants to compile annual OHS Plans stating objectives to be strategically met in accordance with country legislation, Absa OHS policies and supporting documents. Facilitate approvals of the OHS Plan from senior management in-country and attend to queries in regard to the OHS Plan.
  - Assist and advise business on area specific OHS solutions which include; research and development which include the services of technical experts as SABS and occupational hygienists.
  - Maintain the OHS SharePoint site to create continual OHS awareness.
  - Ensure that all contractors and service providers comply with country legislation by auditing their system to ensure that they take responsibility for staff working for them and that they have valid certification or registration and work procedures in place.
  - Monitor OHS implementation at building sites by obtaining and providing information as prescribed by the country (or South African) Construction Regulations which includes the Principal Contractors OHS plan, responsibilities of the Principal contractor, appointments, training, agendas of OHS meeting held, facilities regulations, personal protective equipment etc. Conduct audits of their OHS procedures, do site inspections and attend site safety meetings if required.
  - Manage the Occupational Health & Safety system by sending notifications to Managers and OHS Representatives to submit quarterly reports.
  - Monitor, manage and provide guidance to all Absa workplaces pertaining to this process. Send out a final reminder to workplaces that failed to submit quarterly reports. Obtain final statistics, compile a quarterly report and escalate non-compliance to various stakeholders.
  - Assist in-country consultants to drive compliance by performing audits, inspections and by providing guidance pertaining to appointment of Managers, OHS Representatives, First Aiders, Fire Wardens and Evacuation Leaders.
  - Liaise with Group Learning, Line Managers and Regional or relevant in-country Managers to ensure that OHS teams receive the required training and that all AR workplaces conduct physical emergency evacuations at minimum once per annum as prescribed by their legislation.
  - Monitor changes in country legislation by receiving changes in legislation from in-country OHS consultants and Legal teams. Assist in-country consultants to compile a legal register for their region and facilitate approval from the in-country legal team.
  - Engage in-country OHS consultants for the review of Group OHS policies and supporting documents.
  - Manage business unit queries and specific requirements by assessing the risk and providing guidelines for managing the applicable risk within workplaces, projects and events.
  - Compile monthly and quarterly risk management reports and submit to Line Manager. Review the in-country OHS Consultant compliance reports prior their presentation in the quarterly OHS committee meetings.
  - Escalate non-compliances for OHS System quarterly reports not received, appointments not made and outstanding training requirements to the in-country consultants and People Managers where required.
  - Compile adhoc reports as requested by management.
  - Compile executive-level reports after visiting countries to provide feedback as to the visit and achievements or issues.
  - Work with various internal and external stakeholders to ensure compliance to eliminate or mitigate risks within the Absa Group. By providing statistics and reports pertaining to non-compliances and incidents.
  - Contribute to align policies, supporting procedures and forms to support the prevalent risk reduction and mitigation per workplace.
  - Provide guidance and assistance to eliminate or mitigate risks by making use of internal resources, external experts, and in-country authority or Department of Labour approved service providers.
  - Be conversant with new technology, training requirements, trends and changes pertaining to OHS matters, to be able to provide clients with solutions.
  - Be available by means of e-mail and cell phone to assist internal and external clients with OHS related matters.
  - Provide communication to our audience on Absa Engage and on the OHS SharePoint site.
  - Travel to conduct training, premises conformance tests and workplace inspections on request of management or the client to assess current and emerging OHS issues, and facilitate the upskilling and education of in-country OHS consultants.
  - Attend meetings to represent Group OHS as a supporting function to AR, as well as attend industry related workshops, conferences, seminars and training sessions to become aware of latest trends and changes.
  - Engage in knowledge sharing and collaborative efforts with OHS colleagues and stakeholders.
  - Drive viewer engagement and participation for Group-wide physical and virtual OHS campaigns, to promote OHS content. Assist to collaboratively create and develop content for the OHS campaigns.
Must-have requirements:
  - NQF Level 5 in OHS or equivalent
  - Valid Registration with SACPCMP as a CHSO or Candidate CHSO
  - Risk assessment, risk management experience and OHS experience up to auditing level
  - Incident Investigation certificate or diploma
  - SAMTRAC / Nebosh certificate or diploma
  - 5 years’ experience in the OHS environment in a major institution, preferably in banking industry or construction industry
  - Experience with supervisory and reporting functions
  - Effective communication, written and oral skills
  - Computer literacy in MS Office applications
  - Experience in liaising with external OHS stakeholders
  - Networking with local authorities
  - Strong stakeholder management
  - Good knowledge of the Occupational Health & Safety legislation
  - Audit skills, application of project management methodology and risk management principles
  - Must be proficient in analytical risk identification and measurement, as well as risk response strategies
  - Self-motivated and take ownership
  - Good planning and travel management skills.
  - Ability to implement compliance frameworks
  - Bachelor`s Degrees and Advanced Diplomas: Physical Planning and Construction (Required)
Location: Johannesburg
Team notes: Staff in own area (Manager, Group OHS and in-country OHS consultants); Staff outside own area (other Centre and AR CRES colleagues); Internal customers (OHS Team Members); External customers (Group Wellness, Group Learning, Group Legal, Human Capital); Regulators / Government local authorities; Vendors / suppliers; Other (Industry forums / associations)
Employment equity statement: Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
Accessibility statement: We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Consultant: Occupational Health & Safety

Absa Group

Johannesburg

About us
With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.

About the role
You will implement, monitor and audit Environment, Health and Safety policy, standards and controls across the Absa Group, with a specific focus on Absa building contractors. The role is based in Johannesburg and includes travel to conduct training, premises conformance tests and workplace inspections.

Your team
You report to the Manager, Group OHS and work alongside in-country OHS consultants and other Centre and AR CRES colleagues. You also engage Group Wellness, Group Learning, Group Legal, Human Capital, regulators and local authorities, vendors and industry forums.

What you'll do
• Monitor the OHS management information system by obtaining quarterly reports from all Absa workplaces, sending reminders and final reminders, compiling quarterly statistics and escalating non-compliance to management structures.
• Audit contractors and service providers against country legislation, checking valid certification or registration, responsibility for their staff and documented work procedures.
• Monitor OHS implementation at building sites against the Construction Regulations, covering the Principal Contractor's OHS plan, appointments, training, meeting agendas, facilities regulations and personal protective equipment.
• Conduct site inspections, proactive inspections and investigations such as injury on duty investigations, then report findings with recommendations on technology, procedure, training or disciplinary action.
• Advise Business Units such as CRES, Regional Operations, Group Wellness, Human Capital and Group Learning on the OHS Act and COID, and on risks such as noise levels and facility hazards.
• Assist in-country consultants to compile annual OHS Plans and legal registers, and facilitate approval by senior management and in-country legal teams.
• Support appointment and training of Managers, OHS Representatives, First Aiders, Fire Wardens and Evacuation Leaders, and ensure each workplace runs a physical emergency evacuation at least once a year.
• Compile monthly, quarterly, executive-level and ad hoc risk management reports for your Line Manager, and review in-country consultant compliance reports before quarterly OHS committee meetings.
• Help develop and revise policies, procedures, standards and training material, and present training courses when needed.
• Maintain the OHS SharePoint site and publish content on Absa Engage to drive participation in Group-wide physical and virtual OHS campaigns.
• Attend business unit, region and legislated OHS committee meetings, plus industry workshops, conferences and seminars.

What you need
• NQF Level 5 in OHS or equivalent, and a Bachelor's Degree or Advanced Diploma in Physical Planning and Construction
• Valid registration with SACPCMP as a CHSO or Candidate CHSO
• 5 years' experience in the OHS environment in a major institution
• Risk assessment, risk management and OHS experience up to auditing level, including analytical risk identification, measurement and risk response strategies
• Incident Investigation certificate or diploma, and SAMTRAC or NEBOSH certificate or diploma
• Good knowledge of Occupational Health and Safety legislation, with the ability to implement compliance frameworks

Nice to have
• Experience in the banking or construction industry
• Experience with supervisory and reporting functions
• Experience liaising with external OHS stakeholders and networking with local authorities
• Stakeholder management skills
• Application of project management methodology and risk management principles
• Effective written and oral communication skills
• Computer literacy in MS Office applications
• Planning and travel management skills
• Ability to work independently and take ownership

We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.

Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.

You will need to be reachable by email and cell phone to assist internal and external clients with OHS matters.
